slides.texte_overlay:
Subtle habits that make people
respect you right from the start
Introducing yourself clearly. Full name, eye contact, a calm handshake. People decide how seriously to take you in the first ten seconds.
Not apologising for taking up space. Skip "Sorry, quick question." Just ask. Constant small apologies make people take you less seriously.
Listening to the end before you answer. Interrupting shows impatience. Waiting shows confidence, and people respect a man who isn't in a hurry to talk.
Being honest about what you can deliver. "I can do Friday, not Wednesday." Clear limits earn more respect than promises you can't keep.
Before: people overlooked me in meetings. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and ideas that make people stop and take me seriously.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: people overlooked me in meetings. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Now my ideas make people take me seriously.

slides.texte_overlay: Standing up straight when you talk. Shoulders back, feet planted, hands calm. Your body speaks long before your words do, and people read it in seconds.
Treating your time as valuable. Arrive on time, end meetings when they're done, leave when you said you would. People respect those who respect time.
